string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People\'s Republic of China and one of the world\'s most populous capital cities. Located in northern China, it is governed as a municipality under the direct administration of the State Council. Combining modern architecture with historic sites such as the Forbidden City and the Temple of Heaven, Beijing serves as the nation\'s political, cultural, and educational center. The city has a rich history spanning over three millennia and is the only city in the world to have hosted both the Summer and Winter Olympic Games.

Shanghai is one of the four direct-administered municipalities of China and the most populous urban area in the country. Located on the southern estuary of the Yangtze River, it is a global center for finance, innovation, transport, and international trade. Originally a fishing village and market town, Shanghai grew in importance in the nineteenth century due to its favorable port location. Today, the city is renowned for its iconic Lujiazui skyline, historic Bund waterfront, and extensive public transit system, featuring the world\'s busiest container port.

Chongqing is a large direct-administered municipality in southwestern China, situated at the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers. Known as the Mountain City due to its rugged topography, it covers a vast geographical area with a mix of dense urban districts and surrounding rural counties. Historically a crucial wartime capital during the Second Sino-Japanese War, Chongqing has transformed into a major manufacturing, transportation, and economic hub of western China. The municipality is famous for its dramatic riverfront skyline, monorail transit, and vibrant culinary heritage.

Tianjin is a coastal metropolis in northern China and one of the four national central municipalities. Located on the shore of the Bohai Sea, it serves as a major port gateway to Beijing and a vital hub in the Jing-Jin-Ji metropolitan region. Tianjin developed into a prominent trading port and financial center during the late Qing dynasty, leaving behind a distinctive blend of European-style colonial architecture and traditional Chinese streets. Today, it is a leading center for advanced manufacturing, aerospace industry, shipping logistics, and technological research.
